A factory wants to estimate the percentage of smartphone batteries produced in a day that are defective. A random sample of $420$ batteries from that day was inspected. Based on the sample, it is estimated that $18%$ of all batteries produced that day are defective, with a margin of error of $2.7%$.

Which of the following conclusions about all batteries produced that day is most reasonable?

1. It is plausible that between $15.3%$ and $20.7%$ of the batteries are defective.
2. Exactly $18%$ of the batteries are defective.
3. It is plausible that more than $20.7%$ of the batteries are defective.
4. Exactly $2.7%$ of the batteries are defective.

A city transit agency wants to estimate the percentage of buses that completed their routes on schedule on a particular day. A random sample of $560$ buses from that day was inspected. Based on the sample, it is estimated that $72.5%$ of all buses that day were on schedule, with a margin of error of $3.1%$.

Which of the following conclusions about all buses that day is most reasonable?

1. It is plausible that between $69.4%$ and $75.6%$ of the buses were on schedule.
2. Exactly $72.5%$ of the buses were on schedule.
3. It is plausible that more than $75.6%$ of the buses were on schedule.
4. Exactly $3.1%$ of the buses were on schedule.

:knowledge-point/title: Interpreting the Margin of Error of a Population Proportion
